prior: W-R73 raw-history circular phase canonicalizers failed even to retain intact accuracy. Before designing more complex state-former mechanisms, determine whether shift direction can be statistically identified from raw unlabelled observations, rather than assuming a recoverable phase origin.
hypothesis: Can a learned 3-class phase-origin predictor using a fixed 16-element raw-history state detect intact/+1/-1 shifts on sealed unseen generator and entity identities substantially above 1/3 chance?
freeze: Three predetermined temporal state encoders (levels, first-differences, magnitude) each output 16 scalars. Learn three one-vs-rest ridge weights per candidate on 2592 phase-labelled training events using dev seeds 9008..9023 and generators other than xorshift. Select one with validation seeds 9040..9047 plus 9072..9079, *included* generators/seen entities only. Freeze before exactly one heldout use on 16896..16911, excluded xorshift generator and unseen entity IDs 9..17, 3 sites, 3 amplitudes and 3 balanced phases.
primary: UNSEEN_PHASE_ORIGIN_IDENTIFIABLE iff first-use balanced accuracy >=.45 and per-class recalls each >=.40; PARTIAL_PHASE_IDENTIFICATION iff accuracy >=.37; else NO_PHASE_ORIGIN_IDENTIFIABILITY. Chance=1/3. Predeclare full three-by-three confusion matrix and 3888 heldout labelled observations, no hidden labels in predictor input.
controls: No original shift/label supplied to predictor after training; only 16x4 raw history
Holdout source xorshift excluded from all training and development selection
Validation identity seen, sealed entity IDs 9..17 unseen in training
Each inference uses fixed 16D handcrafted state, three learned 16-weight class scores; extra weights/compute explicitly reported, not same 16-weight baseline
One frozen source first-use and custody-first original artifact, full Go regression and read-only archive verification
Preserve partial and negative outcomes; no paid API, FORGE R32/R33, accepted refs, queue/controller or production
claim_limit: Synthetic supervised phase-origin identification, not learned recurrent memory, general reasoning or RSI.
